title: Japanese Card Grading (2026)
verdict: Japanese card grading in 2026 is simplest at AGS, which grades standard-size TCG cards by laser scan for a flat $18, with eight subgrades and a report.

CGC is the value pick among the large graders at $10 a card in bulk, and a PSA 10 still brings the most on chase cards. TAG gives a strong defect report on modern cards but does not take Yu-Gi-Oh!. Ace Grading is the local choice in the UK.

sections.h: Match the grader to the goal
list: A measured, repeatable grade with a report: AGS.
The highest resale price on a valuable card: PSA.
The lowest fee from a large grader, on cards under $500: CGC.
Subgrades printed on the label: Beckett.
Vintage sports with a traditional following: SGC, then PSA.
A defect map on modern cards it accepts: TAG.
A UK grader for UK and European collectors: Ace Grading.
Whether the card is a standard-size issue. Check oversized promos with the grader.
Back-edge whitening. Even light whitening lowers the grade.
Holo scratches and scuffs across the foil.

ranking.fit: Players and collectors who want Japanese cards back in weeks with the scan to show a buyer.
ranking.lacks: A PSA 10 still sells for more than any other 10 on most chase cards.
ranking.note: TCG bulk tiers are $15, $20 and $30 a card at 20, 10 and 5 business days, from 30 cards. AGS says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

ranking.fit: Card game collectors sending 10 or more cards under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: Value caps on the cheap tiers, and no measured report.

ranking.fit: TCG collectors who value subgrades on the label.
ranking.lacks: 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.lacks: No Yu-Gi-Oh!, and limited capacity in 2026.

why: AGS grades Japanese cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.
Turnaround is counted in days. AGS quotes 20 business days or less from the day your cards are confirmed, with 10 and 5 business day bulk tiers at $20 and $30 a card.

Every card is checked before it is graded. The scan looks for trimming, recoloring and counterfeit print, and each card's digital fingerprint is kept on file so a slab can be verified later by cert number.

faq.a: AGS, PSA, CGC and Beckett all take Japanese-language TCG cards. Japanese cards are standard size, which is what AGS accepts. Check unusual promos or oversized cards with the grader first.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.
Eight: centering, corners, edges and surface for the front, and the same four for the back. They are included in the price and shown in the digital report.

faq.q: Are miscut and error cards graded?
faq.a: At AGS, yes. Miscut and error cards are measured and graded, and damaged cards are not rejected unless they are illegible.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.
